name: ToggleGroup
purpose: Coordinate a related set of single- or multiple-selection pressed commands with shared Brick recipes and Atom keyboard behavior.
useWhen: Related view, formatting, filter, or presentation commands need a visible pressed state and arrow-key movement.

avoidWhen.condition: One independent command toggles, a form submits one required choice, or the selection changes the displayed panel.
avoidWhen.useInstead: Toggle, RadioGroup, or Tabs according to the user job

composition: Compose named Item controls directly inside Root, choose single or multiple value semantics deliberately, and let Root own the shared variant, tone, size, shape, attachment, and width policy.
Use iconOnly only when an Item contains an icon with a complete accessible name; keep visible labels when the icon is not universally understood.

rules.statement: Choose single or multiple mode from the command model and keep the value and onValueChange types consistent with that choice.
Do not use ToggleGroup for a form choice that requires radio semantics, validation, or ordinary form submission.
Give Root an accessible name when surrounding context is insufficient and give every Item a stable complete name.
Give every Item a stable unique value, route controlled changes through onValueChange, and keep string values for single mode and string-array values for multiple mode.
Preserve one roving Tab stop, DOM-order registration, disabled-item skipping, looping policy, orientation-specific Arrow keys, Home/End, and horizontal RTL mirroring.
Use accent or neutral tone for selection emphasis; do not use semantic status colors to imply error, success, warning, or danger.
Choose wrapping, orientation, or an alternative narrow layout without changing DOM order or clipping focus; attached groups do not wrap.
Load styles.css or core.css plus toggle-group.css.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using ToggleGroup as visual tabs, omitting the group name, or styling every Item independently so selected states drift.
commonMistakes.correction: Use Tabs for panels, name the command group, and configure the shared variant and tone on Root.

validation: Check single and multiple values, pressed state, arrows, Home and End, looping, disabled-item skipping, and controlled behavior.
Check wrapping or vertical layout, touch targets, focus visibility, themes, zoom, and RTL.
